title: Turn a Large Goal into the Next Verifiable Step
subtitle: Make the finish condition and dependencies visible.
description: Define the finish condition, expose dependencies, split the goal into observable deliverables, and choose the smallest next step that creates information or progress.

lifeOsSource.hack: Replace a vague large goal with a visible finish condition, a dependency map, and one next deliverable small enough to start.
lifeOsSource.whatYouDo: Write what done looks like, list the major deliverables and external dependencies, split uncertain work until each next step has an observable output, choose the smallest useful step, complete it, and update the map from what you learned.
lifeOsSource.checkIn: What became complete or clearer, what dependency blocks the next step, and what is the smallest observable deliverable now?

faq.question: Should every future step be planned before starting?
faq.answer: No. Map enough to see the finish condition, major dependencies, and next useful action. Update the decomposition as new information changes the plan.
faq.answerHtml: No. Map enough to see the finish condition, major dependencies, and next useful action. Update the decomposition as new information changes the plan.

intro.html: Large goals often hide unclear finish conditions, dependencies, unknowns, and tasks that are still too broad to begin. Decomposition makes those boundaries visible without pretending the first plan will remain correct.

sections.title: 1. Define what done means
sections.html: Write one observable finish condition. Replace labels such as improve the site with a result someone could inspect, check, approve, publish, or use.

sections.title: 2. Map deliverables and dependencies
sections.html: List the few outputs required for the finish condition and mark what depends on another person, decision, system, or unknown.

sections.title: 3. Choose the next verifiable step
sections.html: Break broad work into a deliverable or learning step with a visible result. Complete it, then revise the map and choose the next useful deliverable.

editorialCuration.reason: Replace unsupported completion-rate claims, fabricated experiments, arbitrary duration rules, and broad motivational promises with a concrete decomposition protocol.
